statement: Published data imply a positive above-site (corporate) gold AISC layer in both years, so the payload's l_corp_adj_usd_m of −49 (FY2024) and −8 (FY2025) has the wrong sign, and the FY2024 rounding_bridge_per_oz of 3.51 cannot arise from rounding. Using the 13 site columns (C–F, H–P) of Q4_2025_AISC sheets '2025'/'2024' (row 17 AISC $M, row 18 ounces sold): FY2025 $5,203M on 3,318 koz vs Total Gold $5,428M (MD&A reconciliation) or 1,637×3,318 = $5,431.6M → +$225M to +$229M (+$68–69/oz); FY2024 $5,496M on 3,798 koz vs $5,636M → +$140M (+$37/oz). Sold-weighted regions (P03) give +$202M (+$61.0/oz) and +$124M (+$32.6/oz). The MD&A reconciliation itself carries corporate G&A of $222M (FY2025) and $115M (FY2024) that no site column contains. On the payload's own inputs, ±0.5 rounding of 5,882 and 3,973 moves the ratio by at most $0.31/oz; one $M term moves it by at most $0.126/oz, so 3.51 needs ≥ 28 same-direction terms; 3.51 is 3.5× the ±1-digit tolerance.
scope: corporate-layer and rounding fields of the E676 gold_fy2024/gold_fy2025 blocks; Barrick FY2024/FY2025
inference: Layer = published Total Gold AISC × ounces sold − sum of site (or region) attributable AISC. It is positive in both years under both bases, consistent in sign with E496 (Total Gold layer positive in all 16 quarters, +$23.57 to +$88.66/oz) and E111 (Total Gold above the site/region roll-up).
assumptions: The site columns of sheets '2025'/'2024' (row 17 attributable AISC $M, row 18 ounces sold) or the sold-weighted region rows are the correct comparators.
The sign conclusion holds whether or not the NGM-level column difference is counted in the layer (P00).

The passes report different magnitudes from different comparison bases: P00 and P01, using the 13 site columns of the Q4 2025 AISC workbook ($5,203M on 3,318 koz sold for FY2025; $5,496M on 3,798 koz for FY2024) against published Total Gold × ounces sold, get about +$229M (+$69/oz) and +$140M (+$37/oz); P03, using sold-weighted regions, gets +$61.0/oz (+$202M) and +$32.6/oz (+$124M). statement: By the §21.6 definition (plan lines 4521–4524), for a cell with no applicable identity 'reproduced' reduces to extraction fidelity; this deduction is valid. On the ten known workbooks, 41–46% of numeric cells sit in no instance of the plan's named identities (T1 attributable = ownership × 100%; Σ components, read as T2 flow sums, T6 physical sums and T8 capex; T5 cumulative additivity; T3 sold-weighted roll-up). The figures are 7,784 of P03's 18,860 cells (41.3%), 6,705 of 15,605 site cells (43.0%) and 748 of 1,633 first-publication quarterly M0 per-site fields (45.8%). Whether the 95% bar is then 'met mainly by a correct parser' depends on a reading the plan leaves open. If an identity failure disqualifies only the derived cell, failures remove 0.3–2.0% of cells and a correct extractor clears 95% (ceiling 98.0–99.7%), so the headline mainly measures extraction. If it disqualifies every participating cell, no extractor reaches 95% (ceiling 82.7–94.3%). Under either reading the headline alone hides the identity-checked share, so it should be reported separately. 'Equals the published cell' also needs a reference read independent of the importer, such as BD-271's 3,996 hand-checked cells; otherwise the importer is compared with itself.

definitions.extraction fidelity: the extracted value equals the published cell value

inference: For a cell that is only copied, 'reproduced' proves the parser, not the metric; the §33.1 parity claim is strongest where a number is recomputed from other published numbers.
assumptions: The identity list in the definition (attributable = ownership × 100%, Σ components, Q1 + Q2 = H1, sold-weighted roll-up) is exhaustive as written.
alternative_or_defeater_check: (i) A third reading is possible. Lines 4521–4523 say a cell is reproduced if its value and identities hold, 'or the cell is a discrepancy-register item'; line 4524 then moves only register items with a bridge to 'explained'. Read literally, unbridged (OPEN) register items would count as reproduced, and identity failures registered as OPEN would pass the gate vacuously. The §37.3 restatement (lines 7400–7401) drops the register clause, so the definition is internally inconsistent. (ii) The plan's list leaves out copy identities such as T4 (Minestats = summary) and T18 (AISC workbook = Mine Stats, W1 420/432). They would raise coverage but they test transcription, not the metric. (iii) Two consistent misreads could still pass an identity; NONE_IDENTIFIED_AFTER_BOUNDED_CHECK beyond these.
resolution_or_reversal: The scorer's census of numeric site-quarter cells by identity coverage.
materiality: Moderate: touches the 'vacuous gate' loss and what finance reviewers will be told.
uncertainty: Coverage depends on which families count as 'Σ components' (I counted T2, T6 and T8) and on whether T5 also applies to Minestats flows (I included it). The reading of 'applicable' is the owner's choice and is not an empirical question.

statement: The Q3 2026 workbook is released on 9 Nov 2026 at 06:00 ET (issuer notice dated 9 Oct 2026), 11 days after 29 Oct. It can be shown to third parties as an out-of-sample test of the importer only if two conditions hold before release: a label-anchored Mine Stats importer exists, and its revision is recorded with a time proof the developers do not control. Suitable records are a commit pushed to the public repository, or a built-binary digest with an external timestamp. At HEAD there is no Mine Stats importer. fmine-io/src/xlsx.rs is a generic cell parser with placeholder typing, and its find_rows_by_label helper is used nowhere. The M0 path reads fixed coordinates from file names that do not exist and falls back to an in-code workbook (E725, E677, E678). The M0 binary's JSON has no reproduction, denominator or identity fields. BD-271 already requires the Q3 file to import 'without code changes' but names no record that would prove it. If the importer is completed after 9 Nov, the blind test moves to the Q4 2026 workbook (February 2027). That date falls in M1 (Feb–Apr 2027), outside the M0 window, so GATE-BULL-01's 'must pass on it' wording would have to move with it.
inference: A test is blind only if the tested artefact is fixed before the test data is seen.
assumptions: A label-anchored importer for the ten known vintages can be built within 11 days; if not, the Q4 2026 fallback applies.
alternative_or_defeater_check: Honour-system alternative: nobody opens the Q3 file before the run. It is weaker and is void once anyone opens the file. Feasibility: W1's Python parser (W1 line 130) and this audit's reader both parse all ten vintages with one rule set and no per-file configuration, so an 11-day Rust port is plausible, though not demonstrated.
resolution_or_reversal: A recorded importer digest dated before 9 Nov 2026, or a plan edit naming the Q4 2026 workbook as the blind test.
materiality: Moderate to high: decides whether M0 shows robustness or only fit.
uncertainty: Whether a Rust importer can be frozen within 11 days; whether Barrick posts the workbook on the release day (C051).
original_statement: The Q3 2026 workbook (released 9 Nov 2026) can serve as GATE-BULL-01's out-of-sample test only if a label-anchored importer exists and is frozen, with its revision and binary digest recorded, before release; none exists at HEAD, 11 days before the release. If the importer is written after 9 Nov, the Q3 file becomes in-sample and the plan's only blind layout test is lost unless it moves to the Q4 2026 workbook (February 2027). The plan does not require recording the digest.

statement: Rewrite the M0 FY2026 forecast commitment (§21.6 lines 4495–4496, §37.3 lines 7393–7394, BD-067/068/076) as a scoreable test with four parts. (1) An information cut-off and an input manifest giving each document, its publication date and its sha256. (2) An internal hash deadline fixed now, with 'before the release' kept only as a backstop; per C154, which is not audited here, the release date is announced only about four weeks ahead. (3) Targets on 100%-basis production per site (Mine Stats column B, E456), with a pre-written rule for re-segmentation or ownership change; unit costs are ratios on attributable ounces sold and need their own basis rule. (4) Scoring of the Q4-implied quantity (FY − published 9M) against pre-registered baselines, using the interval score or a bounded-loss PairwiseRace. The baselines are Barrick's per-site guidance as last stated and a naive persistence or run-rate forecast. State also that, with one quarter and about 14 sites, the M0 record demonstrates the protocol, not skill. Acceptance: the hashed record contains the cut-off, manifest, basis, baselines and scoring rule, and the M1 report states skill scores against both baselines, whatever their sign.

Examples: 101 is conservation in the plan but emitted by fmine-crs for a CRS mismatch (the plan maps that guard, G-CRS-1, to 106; fmine-crs CONTRACT maps it to 105); 104 is non-identifiable attribution in the plan, 'Density or specific gravity missing' in the catalog and CalendarWindowMismatch in fmine-time CONTRACT; 301 is the MNPI wall (exit 7) in the plan but is emitted by fmine-numerics for a non-SPD Cholesky matrix (catalog exit 5), and the registry merges both meanings; 303, 304, 401–404, 501 and 502 also diverge, and BD-179 would give 403 a second meaning in one binary. statement: §8.4 lists no refusal code for these cases, but the plan partly answers elsewhere. (a) Usage errors are not refusals: §30.1 gives them exit 2 (line 6579), yet the CLI emits FMINE-REF-401 for an unsupported issuer and a malformed ClaimId (fmine-cli lib.rs lines 180, 252). (b) §29.6 line 6502 routes failed linear solves (kriging, GMRF, reconciliation) to 'FMINE-REF-2xx', so a non-SPD Cholesky belongs in the 2xx family, not 301 as the code has it (fmine-numerics lines 21, 35). (c) §29.6 line 6503 handles LP/MILP failure through the three-gap ledger (§15.2), not a refusal. 304 'LP infeasible' exists only in the registry and catalog, and no code raises it. The open questions are therefore: which code a digest mismatch takes (exit 8 'verification failure' exists, line 6585, but there is no refusal code; the code borrows 502, which the plan defines as stale anchor); which code forecast-ledger mutation takes (the code borrows 403, which the plan defines as moisture/TML); and the exact 2xx number for solver failure.
inference: The borrowed codes collide with planned meanings.
resolution_or_reversal: Owner decision recorded in §8.4.
uncertainty: Whether a new family is preferable to §29.6's 2xx routing is for the owner to decide.
original_statement: Which refusal family covers usage errors, numerical failures (non-SPD matrices, infeasible LPs), digest mismatches and forecast-ledger mutation? §8.4 has none, and the code borrowed 301, 304, 403 and 502.
alternative_or_defeater_check: Defeater found: §29.6 (line 6502) assigns linear-solve failures to the 2xx family. This narrows the question.

For usage errors §30.1 answers it (exit 2, not a refusal), and the defect lies in the code's use of 401. The collision with planned meanings that the claim asserts does hold for 301, 403, 502 and 304.
decision_impact: Narrow the owner question to digest mismatch, forecast-ledger mutation and the specific 2xx code. Fix the CLI to use exit 2 for usage errors.

statement: The question is pivotal but framed too loosely. §7.1 does not name issuer-published workbook values, but its text leans towards `Assertion`: the Assertion row's examples include 'an imported claim' and 'a junior's press release' (line 564). The plan also stores source-document statements as attributed `Assertion` (lines 807, 3560, 5298). `Measured` needs a characterized error model, which a published figure lacks. The code's 'Exact' is not a §7.1 class at all: `fmine-evidence` implements a different five-class lattice (Placeholder, Assumed, Historical, Calibrated, Exact; lattice.rs lines 9–20), and `fmine-public` lines 158–166 label every numeric workbook cell `Exact` + `KnownKnown`. Choosing Assertion has a consequence: it is 'refused as a colour leaf until reviewed' and blocked by G-DISC (line 684). So the owner must decide whether a filed and reconciled issuer number gets an explicit review path.
scope: plan §7.1 and the M0 public lane
inference: The label shown to readers depends on this choice.
resolution_or_reversal: Owner decision recorded in §7.1.
materiality: Moderate: decides the label next to every M0 number.
uncertainty: Whether the owner wants a distinct class (e.g. 'Reported{issuer}') for filed figures is unknown.
original_statement: What §7.1 evidence class does an issuer-published workbook value take: Measured, Derived, or Assertion ('an imported claim', line 564)? §7.1 does not say, and the code chose 'Exact'.
alternative_or_defeater_check: Defeater: the plan's repeated routing of imported or source claims to Assertion is a partial answer the claim did not mention.
audit_resolution_analysis: The premise that §7.1 'does not say' is only half true: the examples and the plan's other uses point to Assertion. The premise that the code 'chose Exact' is true but understates the problem. The code replaced the §7.1 vocabulary rather than picking a class from it.
decision_impact: High for the M0 report label: every number currently carries a class the plan does not define. The owner should decide between Assertion with a reviewed path and a new filed-figure class, and the code lattice should be aligned to §7.1.
audit_execution: rg -n 'Assertion|Measured' over the plan; read of the EvidenceClass enum and the fmine-public Claim construction

statement: On P03's denominator, P03's numbers reproduce exactly. Read so that a failing identity disqualifies every participating cell, a perfect extractor on the ten known workbooks reproduces at most 90.5% (±1 unit) to 92.4% (rounding-aware). With T5 computed rather than bounded the range is 90.2–92.1%; P03's 120-cell bound gives 89.8–91.7%. Under that reading the result holds on every denominator tried: site cells 92.2–94.3%, site three-month first publication 90.7–94.2%, M0 per-site fields 82.7–90.6%. GATE-BULL-01 then cannot be passed. Bridging the NGM and corporate layers raises P03's denominator to 96.8–97.4% (96.5–97.1% with computed T5, about 280–400 cells of slack). On the M0 per-site fields it stays at 92.4–95.6%. The ceiling, however, rests on a reading the plan does not settle. If an identity failure disqualifies only its derived cell, the ceiling is 98.0–98.5% on P03's denominator and 99.1–99.7% on site and M0-field denominators, and the gate is passable. Lines 4521–4524 can also be read as counting unbridged register items as reproduced. 'Cannot be passed as written' is therefore true under one reading only; the robust conclusion is that the definition leaves passability undetermined. The failures are structural (aggregation layers; capitalized interest in total capex), so software quality cannot remove them.

statement: Arithmetic verified. Data gates, reviewers and site access are more likely to bind, and if code does run near sibling rates, the §28.4 80/100/115% triggers would fire within months. original_statement: Code volume will not bind M0–M2 dates: the plan implies about 1,030–1,070 non-blank Rust LOC per calendar day (a 390k phase-A slice in 12 months, §28.3 line 6340; 1,128k in 36 months), equal to the slowest sibling; at sibling rates the 1,298k program ceiling is reached in about 12 months at the median, 3.8 months at Q3 and 1.1 months at the maximum, so either FrankenMining runs at or below the slowest sibling because something other than code binds, or the §28.4 80/100/115% triggers fire within months and BUDGET-AMEND becomes routine. Tests are not a constraint either (about 2,500–3,700 tests implied for phase A).
audit_resolution_analysis: Forecast contract: the horizon (months 0–12), the reference class and a reversal condition are present. The estimand ('binds dates') is vague, and there is no calibration plan or registered scoring rule beyond the reversal test. The arithmetic is exact. The reference-class comparison is the main weakness: most siblings port reference libraries with existing oracles and conformance suites, while FrankenMining is a new domain with external data and human gates. That difference strengthens the 'something other than code binds' branch but makes LOC rates a weak predictor of schedule.
decision_impact: Frame §28/RISK-25 around gates and review capacity rather than LOC throughput; keep the §28.4 triggers.

statement: By the month-12 program gate, no positive real-world calibration claim (that coverage is near the nominal 80% rather than 60–70%) is statistically supportable. Separating 80% from 60% coverage (one-sided α = 0.05, power 0.8) first becomes possible at n = 35 (reject if ≤ 23 covered) and holds for every n ≥ 38 (n = 37 falls short). Separating 80% from 70% needs n = 116 (every n ≥ 127). Expected evidence: FY2026 per-site public forecasts for 14 reporting sites (11 gold, 3 copper; Barrick_Q2_2026_Mine_Stats.xlsx QTD rows 5–29) in one period. With 3–4 metrics each that is 42–56 outcomes, and an equicorrelation ρ = 0.1–0.5 gives n_eff ≈ 2–9. The GATE-TOUCH-05 hindcast and the two forward quarters (BD-209, 'inside the tenancy', line 7925) exist only if site data arrives (P ≈ 0.29, §34.4); if they do, 4–8 scored hindcast quarters and P(both forward quarters covered | calibrated 0.8) = 0.64 add little. Gross miscalibration can still be detected at small n: ≤ 4 covered of n_eff ≈ 9 rejects 0.8 (P = 0.020). Correction to the F7 aside: F7 (line 7203) describes a '90%' interval, and P(≤ 4 of 8 covered | 0.9) = 0.005, so F7's story is strong evidence of miscalibration, not borderline (0.056 applies only to an 80% interval). The plan's `uncalibrated` default and small-sample caveat (lines 7394, 4123, 7482) are consistent with this; GB-38's assumption that a pre-registered scored forecast is persuasive (line 7366, not 7365) rests on an n_eff of a few.
scope: real-world calibration evidence available by month 12
inference: Exact binomial power calculations against the expected outcome counts.
assumptions: The ρ range (common gold-price and cost shocks across sites in a quarter) is assumed.
The hindcast burn-in is at least 4 quarters.
alternative_or_defeater_check: CRPS or interval scores use more information per outcome but cannot certify coverage at n_eff < 10 (agrees with P03). Cross-period independence would raise n_eff only if more periods are scored (C119). The ρ range is an assumption; ρ near 0 would give n_eff ≈ 42–56, still short of 116 and only marginally above 35 for one metric set.
resolution_or_reversal: Count independent scored outcomes at month 12; P03 states the claim reverses if at least 35 exist.
materiality: Medium to high: bounds what may be said to the CFO at month 12 (F7, RISK-07).
uncertainty: ρ and the number of forecast metrics per site are assumptions; the plan does not fix which metrics are forecast.
original_statement: By the month-12 program gate no real-world calibration claim is statistically supportable: separating 80% from 60% coverage (one-sided α = 0.05, power 0.8) needs at least 35 independent outcomes (reject if ≤ 23 covered) and 80% from 70% needs 116, while what will exist is the FY2026 per-site public forecasts (14 reporting sites — 11 gold, 3 copper — and one period; 42–56 site-metric outcomes with within-period correlation ρ = 0.1–0.5 give n_eff ≈ 2–9), the GATE-TOUCH-05 hindcast (8–12 quarters, 4–8 scored after a ≥ 4-quarter burn-in; P(≤ 4 of 8 covered | calibrated 0.8) = 0.056, so F7's 'missed 4 of 8' is itself borderline evidence) and two forward quarters (P(both covered | calibrated) = 0.64). The plan's `uncalibrated` default and small-sample caveat are consistent with this; GB-38's assumption that a pre-registered scored forecast is persuasive (line 7365) rests on an n_eff of a few.
audit_resolution_analysis: All of P03's arithmetic reproduces: 35/23, 116, n_eff 1.95–8.62, 0.0563, 0.64. The 14-site count matches the workbook: 11 gold sites with 2026 values plus Zaldívar, Lumwana and Jabal Sayid; Hemlo and Tongon were sold in 2025. Three corrections. (1) F7's interval is '90%', not 80%. (2) The hindcast and forward quarters are conditional on site data. That strengthens the claim, because with P ≈ 0.7 only public-lane outcomes exist at month 12. (3) 'No real-world calibration claim' is too broad: a negative claim (gross miscalibration) is supportable at small n if the misses are severe. The defensible scope is no positive certification.
decision_impact: At month 12, report forecasts as a track record with the explicit statement 'too few independent outcomes to certify calibration'. A severe miss may be reported as evidence of miscalibration. Fix the F7 aside wherever the 0.056 figure is reused.

statement: Pre-register hashed per-site forecasts with 80% intervals before each Barrick release in the window: Q4/FY2026 (February 2027), then Q1 and Q2 2027 (expected about May and August 2027; the Q3 2027 release falls after month 12). For each vintage, state the as-of date and the forecast horizon. A vintage hashed after a quarter has ended but before its release is a nowcast with respect to operations, so score it separately from vintages hashed before the quarter starts (C026's nowcast problem otherwise repeats each quarter). Every scoring report gives n, an n_eff with its assumed ρ range, and the Clopper–Pearson coverage interval (§37.3 lines 7393–7394, 7412; §21.6 line 4495; BD-067, BD-076). Three periods × 14 sites give 42 site-periods per metric by month 12 instead of 14. That raises n_eff by up to 3× only if forecast errors are independent across quarters; persistent price and cost shocks make the gain smaller. Even tripled (n_eff ≈ 6–27), the evidence stays below the n ≈ 35 needed to separate 80% from 60%, so reports must still say calibration is not certified. Acceptance: at least three forecast sets, each externally timestamped before its release with its as-of date and horizon; each score report states n, n_eff (with ρ) and the coverage interval.
scope: public-lane forecasting from M0 to month 12
inference: Roughly triples n_eff at low cost.
assumptions: Barrick keeps a quarterly release schedule.
alternative_or_defeater_check: Barrick could change its release cadence (bounded: the quarterly cadence held 2024–2026 in the local workbooks and notices). Quarterly per-site forecasts are a new product beyond the M0 FY forecast; scope creep is small because the engine and inputs are the same.

statement: GATE-HELM-02 ('recovers the closed-form EVSI of GB-29-type discrete problems to within 2·SE across 100 seeds', line 4766; BD-227) does not say which reading applies. Every seed within 2·SE passes an unbiased estimator with probability 0.9545¹⁰⁰ = 0.0095. The mean of 100 seeds within 2·SE_mean passes with 0.9545 per problem. At least 90 of 100 seeds within 2·SE passes with 0.994. 'Problems' is plural: over K problems the mean reading passes an unbiased estimator with probability 0.9545^K (0.79 at K = 5, 0.63 at K = 10). P03's proposed fix (mean test AND ≥ 90/100 per problem) gives 0.949^K (0.77 at K = 5, 0.59 at K = 10), so the fix also needs multiplicity control, for example a Bonferroni-adjusted z or a χ² test of the K standardised deviations. No Monte Carlo VOI estimator exists at HEAD: fmine-decide (src/lib.rs line 73) calls the closed-form compute_evsi (crates/fmine-numerics/src/voi.rs line 62), which uses no seeds, yet BD-227 ('VOI estimator vs closed-form EVSI') is closed.
inference: Binomial arithmetic under each reading.
assumptions: Seeds are independent.
alternative_or_defeater_check: Checked whether the gate means a single test problem: GB-29 is one card, but the gate says 'GB-29-type discrete problems' (plural). With K = 1 the multiplicity issue disappears and the claim's fix is adequate.
resolution_or_reversal: Fix line 4766 and BD-227 (P03: 'for each of K test problems, |mean of 100 seeds − closed form| ≤ 2·SE_mean, and ≥ 90 of 100 seeds within 2·SE_seed').
uncertainty: K is not specified anywhere; the severity of the multiplicity defect scales with K.
original_statement: GATE-HELM-02's 'within 2·SE across 100 seeds' (line 4766) does not say which reading applies and fails an unbiased estimator under its literal reading: if every seed must fall within 2·SE, P(pass) = 0.9545¹⁰⁰ = 0.0095; if the mean of 100 seeds must, 0.954; if at least 90 of 100 must, 0.994. The Monte Carlo the gate tests is not yet exercised: fmine-decide computes EVSI in closed form with no seeds (line 73).
audit_resolution_analysis: The three readings and their probabilities reproduce exactly. The code check confirms no seeded estimator exists; compute_evsi is an exact preposterior sum, clamped to [0, EVPI]. The claim calls 'every seed' the literal reading. The more natural reading is the mean one, so the gate is ambiguous rather than failing on its face. The claim's resolution text would install a test that fails a correct estimator 23–41% of the time at K = 5–10, which would itself create a gate that cannot be passed as written (the second-costliest loss class). Closing BD-227 without an estimator is the same pattern as C013.
decision_impact: Rewrite line 4766 and BD-227 with K stated and a multiplicity-controlled criterion. Reopen BD-227 until a seeded estimator exists.

statement: GATE-PLUMB-E5 ('false alarms ≤ α', line 1021) and GATE-CORE-02 (line 1575) give neither the number of null runs nor the test. Tested as a point estimate, a monitor at exactly α passes 54–58% of the time. KILL-PLUMB-6 (line 1026) counts observed false alarms ('more than 1 per site per quarter') summed over the M monitor streams. At about 30 polygons a quarter, each CUSUM stream needs ARL₀ ≥ 30·M polygons for an expected budget of 1 per quarter (600 at M = 20). Because the kill counts observed alarms, an expected rate of exactly 1 per quarter still fires it in 26% of quarters (Poisson); holding per-quarter kill risk to 5% needs an expected rate ≤ 0.36, i.e. ARL₀ ≥ ≈ 85·M. The plan gives no M, CUSUM h or ARL₀.

statement: As the code stands the 9 Nov 2026 Q3 DATA-GATE cannot detect anything: Q3 2026 files are never read (garbage files named barrick-aisc-2026-q3.xlsx and barrick-mine-stats-2026-q3.xlsx leave the output byte-identical to E676), and an absent or unreadable listed file is replaced by the stand-in with exit 0; a listed file whose bytes changed but still inflate, or a valid workbook of the wrong period, is accepted because no sha256 or CRC is checked (only an unparseable file refuses). E676 read no real workbook: an empty workspace reproduces it byte for byte. The plan has no text forcing a fail-closed result on a missing, unregistered or hash-mismatched public-lane source (§21.6 and §31.1 require a sha256 in the registry but no refusal; §21.8 guards G-BULL-1..6 do not cover it), and Appendix F.1 has rows only for software siblings, so the issuer's IR host and its files have no FD row, pin or fallback. Correction to the original wording: GATE-BULL-01's criteria are not 'satisfied' by the substitute (zero uncited numbers fails, and there is no scorer); the point is that no criterion ties a run to registered inputs, and the one that holds (byte-identical reruns) holds equally on a substitute. Extending §27's 'shippable and honest' FD fallback rule (lines 6017-6018) to data is an analogy, not existing plan text.
scope: M0 (Nov 2026–Jan 2027); `fmine assure public --issuer barrick` at HEAD 68e7091 and the plan's controls
inference: Uniform per-file counts equal to the stand-in's, against real files with 3–7 sheets and different counts, imply the E676 run read no real workbook; a new file outside the compiled list is never read.

NONE_IDENTIFIED_AFTER_BOUNDED_CHECK beyond these.
resolution_or_reversal: Reversed if a run on a workspace without the corpus exits non-zero with a typed refusal, or a reproduction shows the E676 counts arising from real files.
materiality: High: a gate that passes vacuously on substituted inputs.
uncertainty: Whether the owner intends the DATA-GATE to be evaluated by the committed command (the claim's assumption) is unstated, but the plan says the importer must meet the Q3 2026 workbook (line 7384-7386).
original_statement: Because a missing or unreadable workbook is replaced by the stand-in and the Q3 2026 file is not in the compiled list (so it is never read, and its layout drift cannot cause a failure), the 9 Nov 2026 Q3 DATA-GATE cannot detect anything as the code stands. The plan has no text forcing a fail-closed result on a missing, unregistered or hash-mismatched source: GATE-BULL-01's acceptance (zero uncited numbers, byte-identical reruns) is satisfied by a deterministic substitute, and Appendix F has foundation rows only for software siblings, so M0's most critical external dependency — the issuer's IR host and its files — has no FD row, pin or fallback rule. statement: The committed deny.toml departs from L-5, and nothing in CI enforces it. Run with cargo-deny 0.20.2 on a scratch crate that depends only on asupersync =0.5.0 (default-features = false), it fails both checks. (1) Licences: four LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider rejections (asupersync, franken-decision, franken-evidence, franken-kernel), because the allow list has no exceptions or clarify. FA's deny.toml at 41363acb carries per-crate exceptions (lines 23–117; asupersync at 61–62) and clarify entries (from line 119). The license-file siblings (fsqlite, frankensearch, fastmcp-rust, fp-*) were not exercised. (2) Duplicates: nine errors (block-buffer, const-oid, cpufeatures, crypto-common, digest, getrandom, rand_core, sha2, syn) under multiple-versions = 'deny' with no skip. getrandom 0.2.17 and rand_core 0.6.4 come via nkeys → rand 0.8; sha2 0.10.9 and digest 0.10.7 come via ed25519-dalek; asupersync itself uses getrandom 0.4.3 and sha2 0.11.0. These are the same pairs FA's deny.toml skips (lines 476–485). (3) Banned crates: tokio enters through asupersync → wasm-bindgen-futures because no [graph] targets is set (P05 missed this). With the tls feature that §31.4(d) needs (line 6831), time 0.3.55 is also banned, via x509-parser/asn1-rs/der-parser. That contradicts L-5 lines 6395–6398 and the 'Fixed' record at Appendix H line 8540. (4) Separately, L-5's petgraph, fastembed and tantivy bans are absent. CI runs no cargo deny (ci.yml; E683). xtask check_deps (lib.rs 300–352, parser 774–807) only compares the direct [dependencies] and [dev-dependencies] key names with the deny list. It has no transitive inversion, licence or one-package-id check, contrary to §31.5 lines 6851–6853, §27.5 line 6189 and L-5 line 6403.

original_statement: The committed `deny.toml` contradicts the plan's L-5 rule and would reject asupersync `=0.5.0` on four counts, and nothing enforces it. (1) Licences: the allow list is MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Unicode-3.0 and Zlib with no exceptions or clarify, while asupersync v0.5.0 (Cargo.toml line 25), franken-decision, franken-evidence and ftui declare `LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider` and fsqlite, frankensearch, fastmcp-rust and fp-* declare only `license-file`; FA's deny.toml at 41363acb (lines 23–80) handles this with per-crate exceptions. (2) Duplicates: `multiple-versions = "deny"` with no skip, while asupersync's non-optional `nkeys = "0.4.5"` pulls getrandom 0.2.17, rand 0.8.7 (rand_core 0.6.4) and, via ed25519-dalek 2.2.0, sha2 0.10.9 (digest 0.10.7), beside asupersync's own getrandom 0.4.3, sha2 0.11.0 (digest 0.11.3) and rand_core 0.10.1. (3) `time` and `chrono` are banned graph-wide, while asupersync's `tls` feature pulls x509-parser → time, §31.4(d) (line 6831) requires QUIC/TLS, and L-5 (lines 6395–6398) bans them for direct dependencies and public APIs only, with a per-foundation allow-list that Appendix H line 8540 records as 'Fixed'. (4) L-5's petgraph, fastembed and tantivy bans are absent. CI runs no `cargo deny` (E683), and `xtask check_deps` (lib.rs 300–352) checks direct `[dependencies]` names only — no transitive inversion, licence or one-package-id check — contrary to §31.5 (lines 6851–6853), §27.5 (line 6189) and L-5 line 6403.

statement: When asupersync enters the graph, the committed deny.toml either fails if wired or, unwired as now, lets the two-package-id failure that §27.5 names pass CI silently. If wired, it fails on licences, duplicates and tokio, and on time once tls is on; all reproduced. The two-source path is reachable through FrankenMining's own pin. §27.5 and franken-stack.lock take asupersync by git rev 78b64636e, fsqlite v0.4.12 (fsqlite-core, fsqlite-btree) takes it from crates.io, and the root Cargo.toml lacks the [patch.crates-io] that §28.6 (line 6412) and BD-001 require. FA never enters the Cargo graph (L-4, subprocess). fsci's consumed crates do not depend on asupersync (only fsci-conformance does). fgdb contributes only if the BD-126 INT-FGDB-001 spike (WP-06, M0–M1) runs in-workspace. The licence failures are not 'unrelated to product risk': they surface RISK-17 (owner and counsel, before M2).

statement: Design option, conditional: a forecast vintage V0 conditioned on H1 2026 public data and hashed before the Q3 2026 release (9 Nov 2026, 06:00 ET, confirmed by the issuer notice) would be a genuine two-quarter-ahead record relative to public information. (3) An external timestamp, for example a published hash; FrozenForecast takes caller-supplied registered_ns. All three are needed within 11 days (29 Oct to 9 Nov 2026). statement: The plan's descriptions of asupersync 0.5.0 defects (a) and (b) (§31.4, lines 6828–6829; RISK-18) match the v0.5.0 source. (a) open_child_region sits in `impl<Caps> Cx<Caps>` and returns a ChildRegion holding a default `Cx` (cap::All); only the runtime-mask SPAWN check refuses. (b) MacaroonKeyRing::verify compares the candidate against an all-zero sentinel when `retired` is None, so an all-zero signature verifies. The (a) and (b) mitigations are adequate, with one caveat: `retire()` resets retired to None, so (b) rests on the FM wrapper that rejects all-zero signatures, not on constructing the ring with a random retired key. The (d) mitigation is not adequate as written. It says the plaintext transport is 'banned by config and check-deps', but `net::atp`, including its TCP session and transfer code, is compiled into the core crate on every native target with no feature gate, so no dependency or feature check can ban it. A code-level lint or a runtime refusal is needed. The enforcement gaps are therefore the closure rules (C150–C152) plus the (d) mechanism.
inference: Source comparison at the pinned tag.
assumptions: The mitigations as written are implemented when asupersync enters.
alternative_or_defeater_check: Alternative: (d)'s 'config' half (an FM-side refusal of plaintext endpoints) carries the control, making the check-deps mention redundant rather than a gap. That still leaves (d) without a CI-enforced test until the plaintext-refusal test (exit 7) exists.
resolution_or_reversal: Re-read §31.4 against the pin when asupersync is admitted.
uncertainty: Defects (c) and (e) were not re-checked at source.
original_statement: The plan's description of asupersync 0.5.0 defects (RISK-18; §31.4) matches the v0.5.0 source for (a) and (b) — e.g. `verify` compares against an all-zero sentinel when `retired` is `None` — and the mitigations are adequate as written; the only gap is enforcement of the closure rules (the deny.toml and admission-record claims).
